title: Human Remains Believed To Be Connected To Victim Of Retired Hurricane Found Years Following Deadly Storm
text:
(Photo by Mario Tama/Getty Images)

Authorities in Tennessee have recovered human remains suspected to be those of an individual killed during Hurricane Helene.

Debris cleanup crews made the discovery near Jackson Island, prompting an active investigation by the Washington County Sheriff’s Office, according to FOX Weather.

Officials suspect the individual perished in the catastrophic flooding triggered by Hurricane Helene almost two years ago. (RELATED: Summer 2026 Breaks All-Time Record For Hottest Ever In United States)

Helene battered the state Sept. 27, 2024, resulting in a disaster declaration that unlocked federal assistance for the hardest-hit counties.

The hurricane roared ashore in the Big Bend region of Florida as a Category 4, packing sustained winds of 140 mph.

Though the system rapidly lost wind intensity after pushing inland, it unleashed relentless tropical downpours and damaging gusts hundreds of miles from the coast, dumping feet of rain across the Appalachians.

Heavy rainfall from Helene’s remnants forced Tennessee’s Nolichucky River over its banks, sending rapid floodwaters coursing through surrounding communities as residents rushed to higher ground, according to East Tennessee State University.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) stated that Helene claimed at least 250 lives across the United States — including a minimum of 175 direct fatalities — solidifying its status as the deadliest hurricane since Katrina in 2005.

For further investigation, officials transferred the remains to the medical examiner.

The news comes amid the National Hurricane Center (NHC) monitoring Tropical Storm Norbert in the Central Pacific Ocean. Potentially headed toward Hawaii, the system currently has maximum sustained winds of 45 mph.
